To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the GAD67 mRNA levels per cell are similar in the thalami of adult rats and adult rats with transplanted neurons, and in the thalamin of rats at different postnatal ages; (b) the GAD mRNA levels per cell increase over time after transplantation and reach adult values during the third postnatal week.

the ectopic location, abnormal connections and lack of segregation from other neurons in grafts of the thalomic reticular nucleus are not associated with abnormal expression of the mRNA encoding GAD67, the key enzyme in GABA synthesis.
the expression of mRNA for the enzyme glutamic acid decaboxylase (GABA-synthesizing enzyme) is normal in ectopically transplanted neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of the development of the thalamocortical system.
the role of GABAergic neurons in the thalami of adult animals.
the role of GABA and GABAA receptors in the control of synaptic efficacy in the hippocampus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transplanted neurons in this study do not develop normally.

the GABAergic nature of the neurons of the thalamus is preserved in the transplanted tissue, and the expression of the GAD67 gene is not affected by the ectopic location, the lack of segregation, the abnormal connectivity or the abnormal morphology of the neurons of this nucleus in the adult host.

the thalamic grafting model provides a valuable tool for the study of the mechanisms involved in the development of neuronal connections and the expression of genes encoding for specific neurotransmitter synthesizing enzymes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thalamic rete nucleus (TRN) is an integral part of the thalaminocortical network, which is essential for the normal processing of information in the cortex.
we have been able to transplant the thalamic nuclei of the thalamus, and the neurons of the reticular nucleus have been able to develop normally despite the ectopical location of the graft.
the GABAergic neurons of the reticular nucleus are not affected by the transplantation and the ectopic environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to transplant neurons from the thalamic nucleus reticularis (TRN), the GABAergic inhibitory nucleus of the thalamus, into the somatosensy thalamus and observe the expression of GAD mRNA.
we can now use the thalamic nucleus as a model to study the development and function of the brain.

the GABAergic neurons of the thalamus, which are normally found only in a restricted area of the thalamo-cortical complex, can survive transplantation in an ectopic position, and that they are able to establish connections with the host tissue, and express the GAD67 mRNA, which is a key enzyme in the GABAergic neurotransmission.
